turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: Three days after my open cholecystectomy, I developed fever and chills with a headache. I also have right-sided chest pain that gets worse when I breathe in and a productive cough that started about 12 hours ago.
Do you feel short of breath or notice any difficulty breathing?
“Yes, I do feel short of breath, especially when I take deeper breaths because the right-sided chest pain gets worse.”
Can you describe the sputum you’re coughing up—its color, consistency, and how much you’re producing?
“It’s been pretty yellow-green, thick, and sticky. I’m coughing up a moderate amount through the day, enough to spit out every time I cough, and it seems to be getting worse.”
Do you know what your temperature has been, or have you measured a fever since the symptoms started?
“I haven’t taken my temperature at home, but I’ve been feeling hot and having chills since it started after the surgery.”
Have you noticed any swelling, redness, or pain in your legs, especially in the calves?
“I haven’t noticed any swelling or redness in my legs, and I don’t have calf pain.”
Do you currently smoke or have you smoked in the past?
“I still smoke—about a pack a day for the past 17 years. I haven’t been able to quit.”
On examination of your chest, do you notice any crackles, wheezes, or decreased breath sounds on the right side?

“I’ve noticed the right side feels a bit more painful, and when you listen I think there may be decreased breath sounds there, but I’m not sure about crackles or wheezes.” “I’m definitely feeling more breathless when I try to take a deep breath because of that right-sided pain.”
Do you have any abdominal pain, swelling, or drainage from your surgical incision since the operation?

I’ve had some discomfort around the incision, but I haven’t noticed any swelling, redness, or any drainage from the site. My main issue has been the fever with chills and the worsening cough with that right-sided pain when I breathe in.
Do you happen to have any recent vital‑sign measurements (temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygen saturation

“I haven’t checked my oxygen saturation at home, but I’ve been feeling very hot with chills and my breathing feels faster since the symptoms started; I don’t know my heart rate or respiratory rate. I did have low blood pressure right after the surgery, but it improved with IV fluids—since then I haven’t measured anything.”

**Question 9:** Can you describe the chest pain in more detail—does it feel sharp or stabbing, is it strictly on the right side, does it get better if you hold a breath or sit up, and does it radiate anywhere (e.g., to the shoulder or back)?

“It’s a sharp, stabbing pain that’s strictly on the right side, and it gets worse when I take a deep breath. I don’t think it improves much when I hold my breath, and it doesn’t really go to my shoulder or back—it's mostly just in the chest area.”
